decisions.choice: Job answers Eliphaz
decisions.reason: Job replies to Eliphaz's third speech (chapter 22), but in chapters 23-24 he speaks less to Eliphaz than about God: where to find him, and why he lets injustice go on. The introduction is prose; the speech (23:2-24:25) is poetry.

decisions.choice: answered (B), said (R), without "and said"
decisions.reason: Hebrew introduces speech with two verbs. Literal keeps both; Balanced and Readable say it once, as in every speech introduction in Job.

records.heading: Job: if only I knew where to find him

records.source: גַּם־הַ֭יּוֹם מְרִ֣י שִׂחִ֑י יָ֝דִ֗י כָּבְדָ֥ה עַל־אַנְחָתִֽי׃
records.gloss: Even today [is] rebellion my complaint; my hand is heavy on my groaning.
pieces: Even today my complaint is defiant; \q the hand on me weighs heavier than my groaning.

L.2: Even today my complaint [is] rebellion; \q my hand is heavy on my groaning.

R.2: Even today my complaint is full of defiance. \q God's hand presses on me harder than my groans can tell.

decisions.choice: rebellion, or bitter
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means rebellion or defiance: Job admits that his complaint defies what his friends say God is doing. Several ancient translations (the Greek and the Syriac among them) read the very similar word "bitter" (compare 7:11; 10:1).

decisions.choice: my hand, or his hand: the hand that weighs on Job
alternatives: his hand is heavy despite my groaning
I press my hand on my groaning (I hold it back)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "my hand is heavy on my groaning", which may mean the hand laid on me, the blow I suffer, is heavier than my groaning can express (compare 19:21, "the hand of God has struck me"). The Greek translation reads "his hand", that is God's. Another reading takes it as Job holding back his groans with his own hand. The first reading is followed here.

decisions.choice: complaint: Job's lament and case
decisions.reason: The word means anxious talk, a complaint poured out (7:13; 10:1; 21:4).

decisions.choice: the hand on me (B), God's hand (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose hand it is according to the reading followed in m2. Literal keeps "my hand".

records.gloss: Who will give [that] I knew and I would find him, I would come to his place!
pieces: If only I knew how to find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q how to come to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} seat!

L.3: Who will grant [that] I knew [how] I might find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q [that] I might come to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dwelling place!

R.3: I wish I knew where to find God, \q so that I could go to the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sits as judge!

decisions.choice: Who will give: if only, I wish
decisions.reason: "Who will give?" is the Hebrew way of saying a strong wish (6:8; 14:4; 19:23).

decisions.choice: his place: his fixed seat, his throne
decisions.reason: The word means a fixed or prepared place. Here it is the place where God sits, where Job could bring his case (verse 4).

decisions.choice: find him: Job wants what Eliphaz told him to do
decisions.reason: Eliphaz told Job to come to terms with God (22:21) and return to him (22:23). Job answers that he would gladly go to God, if he only knew where to find him.

decisions.choice: where he sits as judge
decisions.reason: Readable makes explicit that the place is God's court, as verses 4-7 show.

records.source: אֶעֶרְכָ֣ה לְפָנָ֣יו מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּ֝פִ֗י אֲמַלֵּ֥א תוֹכָחֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: I would set in order before him a case, and my mouth I would fill [with] arguments.
pieces: I would lay out my case before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and my mouth would be full of arguments.

L.4: I would set in order [my] case before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and fill my mouth [with] arguments.

R.4: I would explain my case to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \q and give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all my reasons.

decisions.choice: set in order a case: prepare a legal case
decisions.reason: The words are from the law court: to arrange one's case in proper order before a judge. Job used the same phrase in 13:18.

decisions.choice: arguments: proofs, pleadings
decisions.reason: The word means arguments that set the record straight, the reasoning a person brings to court (13:6).

decisions.choice: give him all my reasons
decisions.reason: Readable says what filling one's mouth with arguments means.

records.source: אֵ֭דְעָה מִלִּ֣ים יַעֲנֵ֑נִי וְ֝אָבִ֗ינָה מַה־יֹּ֥אמַר לִֽי׃
records.gloss: I would know [the] words he would answer me, and I would understand what he would say to me.
pieces: I would learn what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would answer me \q and understand what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would say to me.

L.5: I would know [the] words [with which] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would answer me, \q and understand what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would say to me.

R.5: I would find out how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would answer me, \q and I would understand what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told me.

decisions.choice: I would know ... I would understand: Job's wish
decisions.reason: The verbs have a form that expresses resolve or wish. Job longs not only to speak but to hear God's answer. God does answer him, from the storm (38:1).

decisions.choice: answer: reply in a hearing
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of a reply in court (9:3, 14-16; 13:22).

records.source: הַבְּרָב־כֹּ֭חַיָרִ֣יב עִמָּדִ֑י לֹ֥א אַךְ־ה֝֗וּא יָשִׂ֥ם בִּֽי׃
records.gloss: With greatness of power would he contend with me? No; surely he would set [his mind] on me.
pieces: Would {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} use {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power to argue against me? \q No, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would surely pay attention to me.

L.6: Would {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} contend with me with greatness of power? \q No, surely {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would set [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind] on me.

R.6: Would {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} use all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power to fight me in court? \q No, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would listen to me.

decisions.choice: put on me: pay attention to me
decisions.reason: "Put" with "on" is short for "set the heart (or mind) on", that is, give attention to someone (1:8; 2:3, "have you set your heart on my servant Job?"; 34:14).

decisions.choice: contend: argue a case, bring a lawsuit
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a legal dispute (9:3; 13:19).

decisions.choice: a change of mind from 9:19 and 13:21
decisions.reason: Earlier Job feared that God's sheer power would overwhelm him in court (9:19, 32-35; 13:21). Now he believes that God, if he could be found, would give him a fair hearing.

records.source: שָׁ֗ם יָ֭שָׁר נוֹכָ֣ח עִמּ֑וֹ וַאֲפַלְּטָ֥ה לָ֝נֶ֗צַח מִשֹּׁפְטִֽי׃
records.gloss: There an upright [one] would be reasoning with him, and I would be delivered forever from my judge.
pieces: There an upright person could reason with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and I would be set free by my judge forever.

L.7: There [an] upright [person] could reason with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and I would be delivered forever from my judge.

R.7: There an honest person could present a case to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and my judge would set me free for good.

decisions.choice: upright: straight in conduct
decisions.reason: This is the second word of the pair "blameless and upright" said of Job (1:1). Job means himself: an upright man could argue his case before God.

decisions.choice: delivered from my judge: acquitted for good
decisions.reason: To escape from one's judge is to leave the court cleared. Job is sure that a fair hearing would end in his acquittal, once and for all.

decisions.choice: set free by my judge (B), my judge would set me free (R)
decisions.reason: "Delivered from my judge" could sound as if Job escapes God. Balanced and Readable say what is meant: the judge releases him.

records.source: הֵ֤ן קֶ֣דֶם אֶהֱלֹ֣ךְ וְאֵינֶ֑נּוּ וְ֝אָח֗וֹר וְֽלֹא־אָבִ֥ין לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Look, forward I go, and he is not [there]; and backward, and not I perceive him;
pieces: I go to the east, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is not there, \q to the west, and I cannot make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out;

L.8: Look, I go forward, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is not [there], \q and backward, and I do not perceive {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}};

R.8: I look in the east, but God is not there. \q I look in the west, but I cannot find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: forward and backward: east and west
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the directions are named facing the sunrise: "in front" is east, "behind" is west, the left hand is north and the right hand south (verse 9). Job searches every direction (compare Psalm 139:7-10, where the psalmist cannot escape God).

decisions.choice: look: but the fact is
decisions.reason: The word calls attention to what follows, in contrast to the hope of verses 3-7: God cannot be found.

decisions.choice: east, west
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the compass directions the Hebrew words mean; Literal keeps "forward" and "backward".

records.source: שְׂמֹ֣אול בַּעֲשֹׂת֣וֹ וְלֹא־אָ֑חַז יַעְטֹ֥ף יָ֝מִ֗ין וְלֹ֣א אֶרְאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: [On the] left when he works, and not I behold [him]; he turns [to the] right, and not I see [him].
pieces: in the north, where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is at work, I do not see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turns to the south, and I have no sight of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.9: [On the] left, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is at work, I do not behold [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}]; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turns [to the] right, and I do not see [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}].

R.9: God is busy in the north, but I cannot see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q He turns to the south, but I still do not see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: left and right: north and south
decisions.reason: See verse 8: facing east, the left hand is north and the right hand is south.

decisions.choice: turns: or hides himself
alternatives: he hides himself in the south
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to turn aside or to wrap oneself up. It may mean that God turns to the south, or that he hides himself there. Either way Job cannot see him.

decisions.choice: when he is at work: God is active, but unseen
decisions.reason: Job does not doubt that God is at work in the world; what he cannot do is see him (9:11).

decisions.choice: north, south
decisions.reason: As in verse 8, Balanced and Readable give the compass directions.

records.source: כִּֽי־יָ֭דַע דֶּ֣רֶךְ עִמָּדִ֑י בְּ֝חָנַ֗נִי כַּזָּהָ֥ב אֵצֵֽא׃
records.gloss: For he knows [the] way [that is] with me; [when] he has tested me, like gold I will come out.
pieces: Yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows the road I am on; \q when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has tried me, I will come out like gold.

L.10: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows [the] way [that is] with me; \q [when] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has tested me, I will come out like gold.

R.10: But God knows every step I take. \q When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has finished testing me, I will come out like gold that has been refined.

decisions.choice: for, or yet: God knows, even though Job cannot see him
decisions.reason: The word joins this verse to verses 8-9: Job cannot find God, but God knows all about Job. It can be read as "for" or as "but"; Balanced and Readable bring out the contrast.

decisions.choice: the way with me: my conduct, the course of my life
decisions.reason: "The way with me" is the way Job walks, his conduct. God knows it fully, and Job is confident it will stand the test (verses 11-12).

decisions.choice: tested like gold: proved genuine by fire
decisions.reason: The verb is used for testing metal in the furnace to show what is pure (Zechariah 13:9; Psalm 66:10; Proverbs 17:3). Job is sure that God's testing would show him to be pure.

decisions.choice: gold that has been refined
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of coming out as gold means (m3).

records.source: בַּ֭אֲשֻׁרוֹ אָחֲזָ֣ה רַגְלִ֑י דַּרְכּ֖וֹ שָׁמַ֣רְתִּי וְלֹא־אָֽט׃
records.gloss: In his step has held fast my foot; his way I have kept and not I have turned aside.
pieces: My foot has held to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} footsteps; \q I have kept {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way and not turned away from it.

L.11: My foot has held fast to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} steps; \q I have kept {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way and have not turned aside.

R.11: I have followed right behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q I have stayed on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} path and never left it.

decisions.choice: held fast to his steps: followed God closely, obeyed him
decisions.reason: To walk in someone's steps is to follow where they lead. Walking in God's way means obeying him (Psalm 17:5; 44:19).

decisions.choice: Job claims what Eliphaz denied
decisions.reason: Eliphaz charged Job with keeping "the old path of the wicked" (22:15). Job answers that he has kept God's way.

decisions.choice: followed right behind him
alternatives: my foot has held fast to his steps
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture of walking but in everyday words.

records.source: מִצְוַ֣ת שְׂ֭פָתָיו וְלֹ֣א אָמִ֑ישׁ מֵ֝חֻקִּ֗י צָפַ֥נְתִּי אִמְרֵי־פִֽיו׃
records.gloss: [The] commandment of his lips, and not I have departed; more than my portion I have treasured [the] words of his mouth.
pieces: From what {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} lips commanded I have not turned back; \q I have stored up the words of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth above the food I live on.

L.12: [From the] commandment of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} lips I have not departed; \q more than my [own] portion I have treasured the words of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth.

R.12: I have always obeyed what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded. \q I have treasured {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words more than the food I eat.

decisions.choice: my portion: my allotted food
decisions.reason: The word means what is set or allotted to someone; with food it is one's daily portion (Proverbs 30:8, "the bread of my portion"; Genesis 47:22). Job valued God's words more than what kept him alive. The ancient Greek translation has "in my bosom", which would need a slightly different Hebrew word; another reading is "more than my own rule".

decisions.choice: treasured: stored up as precious
decisions.reason: The verb means to hide away something valuable (Psalm 119:11, "I have treasured your word in my heart").

decisions.choice: the stray "and"
decisions.reason: The line reads "the commandment of his lips, and I have not departed". The "and" is unusual; the sense is clear: Job has not turned away from God's command.

decisions.choice: the food I live on
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "my portion" means here (m1).

records.source: וְה֣וּא בְ֭אֶחָד וּמִ֣י יְשִׁיבֶ֑נּוּ וְנַפְשׁ֖וֹ אִוְּתָ֣ה וַיָּֽעַשׂ׃
records.gloss: And he [is] in one, and who can turn him back? And his soul desires, and he does.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is of one mind, and who can turn {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} back? \q Whatever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} desires, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does.

L.13: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] in one [mind], and who can turn {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} back? \q What {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} soul desires, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does.

R.13: But once God has decided, no one can change {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind. \q He does whatever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants.

decisions.choice: in one: of one mind, unchangeable
decisions.reason: The phrase is literally "he is in one". It most likely means God is single in purpose, and once he has decided no one can turn him. Some take it as "he is unique, alone"; others change one letter and read "he has chosen". The point is the same: God's will cannot be resisted.

decisions.choice: his soul desires: he wants
decisions.reason: "Soul" (nefesh) here means the self with its desires, so "his soul desires" is "he wants" (Psalm 115:3 says God does whatever he pleases).

decisions.choice: but: Job's confidence meets God's freedom
decisions.reason: After Job's certainty that he is innocent (verses 10-12), this verse turns: God is free to do what he has decided, and Job cannot change it.

decisions.choice: once God has decided, no one can change his mind
alternatives: he is one, and who can turn him back
decisions.reason: Readable unpacks "he is in one" and "who can turn him back" into one plain sentence.

records.source: כִּ֭י יַשְׁלִ֣ים חֻקִּ֑י וְכָהֵ֖נָּה רַבּ֣וֹת עִמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: For he will complete my decree, and like these, many [are] with him.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will carry out what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has decreed for me, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has many more decrees like it.

L.14: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will complete what is decreed for me, \q and many such [things are] with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.14: He will do to me what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has planned, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has many more plans like it.

decisions.choice: my decree: what is decreed for me
decisions.reason: The word is the same as "my portion" in verse 12: what is set or allotted. Here it is what God has appointed for Job, including his suffering (14:5, 13, a set limit).

decisions.choice: many such things with him: God has more in store
decisions.reason: "Like these, many are with him" means that God has many such decrees in mind; Job fears more of the same.

decisions.choice: he has many more decrees like it
alternatives: many such things are with him
decisions.reason: Balanced turns "many [are] with him" into an English sentence with God as subject.

records.source: עַל־כֵּ֭ן מִפָּנָ֣יו אֶבָּהֵ֑ל אֶ֝תְבּוֹנֵ֗ן וְאֶפְחַ֥ד מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: Therefore from before him I am terrified; I consider, and I am in dread of him.
pieces: So I am terrified in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence; \q when I consider, I dread {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.15: Therefore I am terrified before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q I consider, and I am in dread of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.15: So I am terrified of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q the more I think about it, the more afraid I become.

decisions.choice: terrified: dismayed, shaken
decisions.reason: Eliphaz said that dread terrified Job because of his sins (22:10, the same verb). Job says it is God himself who terrifies him (verse 16).

decisions.choice: I consider: the fear grows from thinking it through
decisions.reason: The verb means to look closely or reflect. When Job thinks about God's unchangeable will (verses 13-14), his fear grows.

records.gloss: And God has made soft my heart, and [the] Almighty has terrified me.
pieces: God has weakened my heart; \q the Almighty has filled me with terror.

L.16: And God has made my heart faint, \q and the Almighty has terrified me.

R.16: God has made me lose courage; \q God All-Powerful has frightened me.

decisions.choice: made my heart soft: took away my courage
decisions.reason: A "soft" or faint heart is one without courage (Deuteronomy 20:3, 8; Isaiah 7:4).

decisions.choice: God, the Almighty (El, Shaddai)
decisions.reason: The two names stand in parallel, as often in Job. See 5:17 on Shaddai.

decisions.choice: made me lose courage
decisions.reason: Readable says what a faint heart means.

records.gloss: For not I have been silenced before darkness, and before my face he has covered gloom.
pieces: Yet it is not darkness that has silenced me, \q nor the deep gloom that covers my face.

L.17: For I have not been silenced because of darkness, \q nor [because] gloom has covered my face.

R.17: It is not the darkness around me that has silenced me, \q nor the deep gloom that hides my face.

decisions.choice: a hard verse: what silences Job is God, not the darkness
alternatives: yet I am not silenced by the darkness
if only I had vanished in the darkness
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is difficult. The reading followed here joins it to verses 15-16: it is God who terrifies Job and makes him faint, not the darkness of his suffering. Other readings: "I am not silenced by the darkness" (Job keeps speaking in spite of it); or, changing "not" to a word for a wish, "If only I had vanished in the darkness, and gloom had covered my face" (as in 3:3-10; 10:18-19).

decisions.choice: silenced: put to silence, destroyed
decisions.reason: The verb means to put an end to, to destroy, or to silence (6:17, of streams that dry up).

decisions.choice: darkness, gloom: suffering, and the death it threatens
decisions.reason: Darkness and deep gloom are pictures of disaster and death (10:21-22; 22:11, where Eliphaz used darkness of Job's punishment).

decisions.choice: it is not darkness that has silenced me
alternatives: I have not been silenced by darkness
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put "not" with "darkness", so the sentence says clearly what does not silence Job (m1).
